assessment: One cost governs this deck: {W}{U}{B}{R}{G}, with no generic to pay around. Four cards in the 99 spend it and one produces it, so the deck buys one activation a turn and both its engine and its kill want more. Six of the ten below buy a second payment; the other four close the land class nothing in the 99 answers, add a finisher the count can see, and put a second, structurally different kill on the table. Two famous cards are deliberately absent: Gaea's Cradle, because raw mana volume is a strength here at 55 sources and colour is the constraint, and The One Ring, because the card-advantage axis reads under only in the taxonomy.

combo_lines_opened.produces: Put a selection of creature cards from your library onto the battlefield
Infinite combat phases, infinite creature tokens with haste, infinite untap of creatures

ten.why: Every Sisay activation puts a creature onto the battlefield, and Intruder Alarm turns that entry into an untap of Bloom Tender, Faeburrow Elder, Relic of Legends and Jegantha — the fetch pays for the next fetch, which is the one thing the deck cannot do today.
ten.unlocks: Chained activations inside one turn, with five separate in-deck partners for the Sisay half and a Najeela line on top; the price is its first line, since your own dorks then stop untapping in your untap step and every opponent's creatures untap on each entry.

combo_lines_opened.produces: Infinite ETB, infinite colored mana, infinite creature tokens with haste, infinite blinking

ten.why: Two mana on turn two gives all 39 creature copies '{T}: Add one mana of any color', so the 4.066 bodies the goldfish has on board by turn six become the five distinct pips Sisay's activation demands.
ten.unlocks: A five-pip battery assembled out of bodies you were deploying anyway, plus an Emiel line with both halves cheap; unlike Esika it carries no legendary clause and unlike Katilda no Human clause.

combo_lines_opened.produces: Infinite combat phases, infinite creature tokens, infinite ETB, infinite lifegain

ten.closes: engine component: the loop's per-combat cost
ten.why: The deck's kill re-buys {W}{U}{B}{R}{G} every combat and the deck can afford it once; Bear Umbra untaps all lands on the attack trigger, before the activation is due, so the toll is paid each iteration rather than once.
ten.unlocks: The verified Najeela combat loop stops being a board-state win and starts being a two-card one, and Umbra armor absorbs the first destroy aimed at whichever body wears it.

combo_lines_opened.produces: Infinite untap of legendary creatures you control, infinite mana legendary creatures you control can produce

ten.why: Marvin borrows Ioreth's '{T}: Untap two other target legendary creatures', and at mana value 2 he is legal the moment one colour sits beside Sisay — power 3, the second rung of the ladder — so this is the rare mana line the tutor can go and get.
ten.unlocks: An untap engine aimed straight at Jegantha, Bloom Tender, Faeburrow Elder and Relic of Legends, with the half you have to draw already sleeved.

ten.why: 'Lands you control have "{T}: Add one mana of any color"' makes all 40 land copies produce every pip, including Plaza of Heroes, Secluded Courtyard and Unclaimed Territory, and it costs {3} so no colour has to exist before it lands.
ten.unlocks: A five-colour mana base that does not need a board first, which is what separates it from Bloom Tender and Faeburrow Elder; note the colour-sources axis will not move, because manabase counts sources per card and cannot read a static grant.

ten.card: Vito, Thorn of the Dusk Rose

cards: Vito, Thorn of the Dusk Rose
combo_lines_opened.produces: Repeated life loss for one opponent from the combat loop's lifelink

ten.why: Najeela's activation hands every attacker lifelink, and Vito turns each of those life gains into life loss for a chosen opponent, so a loop that currently needs five creatures to connect with a player can instead kill through a wall of blockers.
ten.unlocks: A finisher the count can actually see — recomputed over the 99 with Vito added, threat-density goes 3 to 4 — on a mana-value-3 legend Sisay reaches at power 4, two colours in.

ten.why: Black is the pinch at 21 sources against a 36 target, and 'Each land is a Swamp in addition to its other land types' makes every one of the 40 land copies produce the {B} that Sisay's and Najeela's activations both demand.
ten.unlocks: A live fetch on the cold-start turn as well — the deck runs zero legendary lands, so at base power 2 only three cards are legal targets, and this is a fourth that does work the moment it arrives.

ten.why: Land is the one permanent class no card in the 99 answers — Path to Exile is creature-only, Loran reaches artifacts and enchantments, Toxic Deluge is creatures — and 'Destroy target permanent' covers it at instant speed for three mana.
ten.unlocks: Recomputed over the swapped 99, interaction-breadth goes 3 classes to 4, with land 0 to 1; the 3/3 it hands back is the price, and against a Cabal Coffers or a Field of the Dead it is cheap.

combo_lines_opened.produces: Infinite mana of colors among permanents you control

ten.why: Four cards already in the 99 pair with it — Bloom Tender, Faeburrow Elder, Selvala and the Kinnan plus Birds of Paradise pair — and with three colours on board a Bloom Tender wearing it nets mana every untap, which is the second and third activation in one card.
ten.unlocks: The deepest redundancy available for the five-pip bill, at the cost of being an Aura on a creature: it is a two-for-one to any spot removal, which is why the deck's Heroic Intervention matters more once it is sleeved.

ten.why: The deck's kill is one assembly, so answering the assembly answers the deck; Heliod, Sun-Crowned is already sleeved and Sisay fetches him at power 4, which makes Ballista half of a second kill that shares nothing with the combat loop.
ten.unlocks: A damage-based out against the fog, the wall of blockers and the extra-combat hate that beat Najeela — and short of the kill it is repeatable removal in a suite sitting exactly on Walser's floor of 8. Note that it carries no wincon role, so the threat-density count does not move.

gaps: Every line above is a candidate. Only stacks/002 (Najeela plus Derevi) carries a passing checker verdict in this deck, and its own final state calls the pair not self-contained. The four highest-leverage scenarios to settle are Bear Umbra plus Najeela, Marvin plus Ioreth, Intruder Alarm plus Sisay plus a mana body, and Walking Ballista plus Heliod.

Vito plus Najeela is read off oracle text, not off a combo record: Najeela's activation grants lifelink to attacking creatures and Vito converts life gained into life lost for a target opponent. No entry in the combo data pairs them, so treat it as the least-grounded line here until a stack scenario runs.

Bear Umbra, Nature's Will and Sword of Feast and Famine are three interchangeable answers to the same per-combat toll, each with a two-card record against Najeela. Bear Umbra is listed because its trigger is on attack rather than on damage and its Umbra armor covers the body; the other two are equally defensible and one slot, not three, should be spent.

Chromatic Lantern and Urborg both make mana the right colours without moving the colour-sources axis, because manabase counts sources per card and models no static grant. The axis is the wrong instrument for a static land grant, and nothing in the repo currently measures the thing they actually fix.

strategy.md has no section on toolbox construction or on treating library access as the resource a deck spends, so the ranking of fetchable picks over drawn ones — Marvin, Vito and Urborg over Intruder Alarm and Cryptolith Rite on that dimension alone — rests on the ladder arithmetic in this deck's own artifacts, not on cited principle. strategy:deckbuilding.redundancy-vs-tutors does ground the shape of the list: 'So stack the classes you want every game (ramp, draw, removal, enablers), tutor only the irreplaceable.'
No deck recon for this commander, so nothing here is weighed against what strong Sisay lists actually run; every pick is grounded in this deck's own audit, engine block and combo containment.
